title: Electromagnetism
standard_text: The electromagnetic force produces both electricity and magnetism: static and current electricity, electromagnets, and generating electricity (generators and turbines, including BC's hydroelectric dams). (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 7, Physics)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 science worksheets (BC): electric charge, circuits, magnets, electromagnets, and how generators make electricity. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Moving charges make magnetism; moving magnets make electricity.
key_sub: Most of BC's electricity comes from hydroelectric dams.
body_html:
How to think about it

Electric current is a flow of charge. A wire carrying a current makes a magnetic field; wrapping the wire into a coil around iron makes an electromagnet, which can be turned on and off.

Moving a magnet near a coil of wire makes a current flow: this is how generators work. In a hydroelectric dam, falling water spins a turbine, which turns a generator. Most of BC's electricity is made this way.

Example

How can you make an electromagnet stronger?

More turns of wire or more current

Answer: add more coils or more current

Example

What spins the generator in a hydroelectric dam?

Falling water

Answer: a turbine turned by water

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a magnet makes current when it stays still.
  • Thinking generators make energy from nothing.
  • Mixing up static and current electricity.

items.q: How does an electric guitar pickup work?
